core: opening a text file for reading

claims.claim: Python's open() returns a file object; text files read through it produce strings.
Using a with statement to open a file closes it when the suite finishes, including when an exception occurs.
read() reads the remaining contents, while readline() reads one line and returns an empty string at end of file.
Iterating directly over a file object is a simple, memory-efficient way to process its lines.
When the intended text encoding is UTF-8, Python documentation recommends specifying encoding='utf-8' explicitly because defaults can be locale-specific.

In text mode, Python translates platform-specific line endings to 
 when reading.
